name: Helix Corp Standard Cubicle Day Set
description: A mass-produced Tier 3 office uniform that announces its wearer's station with quiet, merciless precision. The core is a Helix Corp-issued slim-fit trouser in mid-grey polyblend with a faint institutional sheen — pressed but never quite crisp, the fabric holding a ghost crease from the last hundred wearers before it was laundered and reissued. Paired with a Stratum-branded poplin button-down in pale corporate blue, the collar slightly too stiff, the cuffs slightly too short, the whole garment a fraction off in every dimension as though tailored for a statistical average person who doesn't exist. A thin synthetic-leather belt in charcoal, a clip-on ID badge lanyard in Helix Corp teal, and Huxley Quietstep loafers in scuffed black round out the look. The ensemble carries the particular exhaustion of clothes worn five days a week, dry-cleaned on the company's schedule, returned to the locker on Friday and retrieved Monday morning. No ornamentation, no personalization — any attempt at individuality, a pin, a colored lace, a visible tattoo, has been quietly flagged by HR.
functionality: ID badge integration, standard BCI port access collar notch, anti-static lining for proximity to server equipment, stain-resistant coating on trouser front panels
what_it_says: You are a cog and you know it. You have internalized the dress code. You have stopped fighting. The badge around your neck tells security where you're allowed to go, and the outfit tells everyone else you're allowed nowhere interesting.
worn_by: anyone on a provisional contract hoping to go permanent
manufacturer: Helix Corp Internal Procurement Division — issued, not purchased
story_hooks: A character wearing this uniform discovers that their badge lanyard has been quietly downgraded — they can no longer access the floor they've worked on for three years. No explanation. No email. Just a red light on the reader.

Someone has been wearing this exact uniform for eleven years. Today they notice a small handstitched mark inside the collar — not theirs. They recognize the stitch pattern as belonging to someone who died in the building six years ago.

A player character needs to move through a Helix Corp office without being flagged. Acquiring this uniform is step one — but the biometric weave embedded in the badge lanyard is step two, and that's where things get complicated.

physical_description.visual_profile: A figure rendered almost invisible by institutional uniformity — the silhouette of competent mediocrity. Slim-fit trouser meets slightly-too-stiff button-down in a palette of greys and pale blues that seem to absorb personality. The overall impression is of someone who has been filed away into a corporate filing system and retrieved on schedule.
physical_description.fit: Slim but not fashionable — tailored to a statistical mean that fits no actual body perfectly. The shirt cuffs sit a half-inch too short on the wrists; the trouser break is meticulous but impersonal. Compression without comfort.
physical_description.primary_material: Mid-grey polyblend trousers with institutional sheen; pale corporate blue poplin shirt; synthetic-leather belt in charcoal; scuffed black synthetic loafers
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly plasticky finish from repeated industrial laundering. The shirt has the crisp-but-brittle quality of overstarched institutional wear. The trouser fabric holds a ghost crease that never quite disappears. The loafers show organized wear — scuffs that follow a predictable pattern.
physical_description.color_scheme: Institutional grey, pale corporate blue, charcoal, black. Accent of Helix Corp teal on the ID lanyard. No pattern — pure, flat, demoralizing color.
physical_description.closures: Standard button-down shirt front; trouser zip and hook-and-eye; leather belt with standard buckle; clip-on lanyard for ID badge (friction-fit, designed to be ripped away if caught in machinery)
distinctive_features: Clip-on ID badge lanyard in Helix Corp teal — non-negotiable, visible at all times
Collar slightly too stiff, suggesting poor fit or over-processing
Cuffs slightly too short, revealing a fraction of wrist
Belt worn smooth in specific places by thousands of previous wearers
Loafers scuffed in a pattern consistent with cubicle-to-elevator-to-cubicle movement
No visible pockets that weren't standard issue
Faint institutional laundry mark on inner collar
Trouser crease that holds memory of previous wearers
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — Working class corporate drone. Not poverty, but unmistakable institutional servitude.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is a Helix Corp mid-level functionary, middle manager, or administrative support. No autonomy in clothing choice. The outfit signals compliance, predictability, and the complete sublimation of individual identity into corporate function. Wearing this marks you as someone who has internalized the corporation's values — or at least their dress code.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but never comfortable. Pressed weekly but never quite fresh. The fabric shows organized wear in the crotch and seat from sitting eight hours a day. The collar begins to fray slightly by Thursday. The loafers develop a toe scuff by mid-week. Everything is functional, nothing is new, everything suggests a person being slowly worn down by their own uniform.
